definitions.explanation: An open-air market held in the early morning, typically selling fresh produce, seafood, and local goods. A traditional feature of many Japanese towns and cities.

examples.japanese: {朝市|あさいち}で{野菜|やさい}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought vegetables at the morning market.

examples.japanese: {毎週|まいしゅう}{日曜日|にちようび}に{朝市|あさいち}が{開|ひら}かれる。
examples.english: A morning market is held every Sunday.

examples.japanese: {旅行先|りょこうさき}で{地元|じもと}の{朝市|あさいち}を{訪|おとず}れたら、{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚介類|ぎょかいるい}や{手作|てづく}りの{漬物|つけもの}が{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: When I visited the local morning market at my travel destination, fresh seafood and handmade pickles were lined up for sale.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Morning markets are a long-standing tradition in Japan, especially in rural and coastal areas. Famous examples include the {輪島|わじま}{朝市|あさいち} (Wajima Morning Market) in Ishikawa Prefecture and the {函館|はこだて}{朝市|あさいち} (Hakodate Morning Market) in Hokkaido. They are popular tourist attractions and a way for locals to buy fresh, seasonal produce directly from farmers and fishers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朝市|あさいち}に{行|い}く: to go to the morning market
- {朝市|あさいち}が{開|ひら}かれる: a morning market is held
- {朝市|あさいち}で{買|か}い{物|もの}する: to shop at the morning market

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マルシェ: marché (farmers' market, loanword from French)
- {市場|いちば}: market (general)
